newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco holds forum on Mediterranean development.
newsitem.headline: Morocco holds forum on Mediterranean development.

text.p: More than 400 delegates from public and private sectors met on Monday in Morocco for the start of a six-day forum to discuss development issues in the southern Mediterranean countries, a World Bank spokesman said.

Sponsored by the World Bank, the forum will bring delegates together in 12 workshops to exchange views on the role of information, knowledge and technology in the region's economic development, the spokesman said.

"For the first time, managers and government officials from Middle East and North Africa, will have the chance to exchange their experiences on daily management and policies to respond to the development challenges," the spokesman said.
The forum is in the Moroccan southern city of Marrakesh.

The World Bank vice-president for Middle East and North Africa Kemal Dervis and Vinod Thomas, director of the Bank's Institute of Economic Development are among the participants to the meeting, he added.

Among the subjects the delegates will examine are banking services, micro-enterprises financing, investments, telecommunications, infrastructure upgrading, the state role in development and World Trade Organisation and the Mediterranean.
The forum will end on May 17, officials said.
